red-autumn-calville.heading: 4. CALVILLE ROUGE D'AUTOMNE.
red-autumn-calville.flavour: Flesh: white, tinged with red under the skin, and very much so on the side exposed to the sun; it is tender, delicate and juicy, with a pleasant vinous and violet scented flavour.
red-autumn-calville.quality: An apple very highly esteemed on the continent both as a culinary and dessert fruit
red-autumn-calville.storage: It is in season during October and November.
red-autumn-calville.climate: it requires a favourable season in this country to maintain its best qualities.
red-autumn-calville.note: Syn: Autumn Calville; Autumn Red Calville.

coccagee.heading: 6. COCCAGEE.
coccagee.flavour: Flesh: yellowish white, firm and crisp. Juice: moderately plentiful, of an amber colour, and a harsh austere taste. It is so extremely rough and tart that it would be almost impossible to eat one raw.
coccagee.quality: A very old and highly esteemed variety for culinary purposes, and especially for baking, when it possesses a peculiarly rich flavour.
coccagee.storage: It is in season from October, to February and March.
coccagee.note: Believed Irish; favourite Devon cider apple c.1800. Stafford (1753) found in its cider 'a vinous pipinary golden flavour'. Juice 9.08% sugar. 'Rough and tart' is Brookshaw quoted.

styre.heading: 8. FOREST STYRE.
styre.flavour: Flesh: yellow, dry and harsh. Juice: small in quantity, pale straw colour, changing to deep amber, with a remarkably sweet luscious flavour and some astringency.
styre.quality: A fine old Gloucestershire cider apple
styre.climate: extensively cultivated on the thin light limestone soil of the Forest of Dean.
styre.note: Syn: Stire; Stirom. Juice 14% sugar, 3.3% tannin etc. Knight: affords a stronger cider than any other apple. Remarkably sweet juice sits uneasily with our 'sharp' tag, though acidity is not mentioned. The book also has a separate short 'Styre, or Small Styre' (line 10853), a small red apple.

woodcock.heading: Woodcock.
woodcock.quality: It was formerly held in great esteem
woodcock.note: Short paragraph in the list of Herefordshire cider apples: figured by Knight; disappeared from orchards and the fruit exhibited was not true to character. Not the Sussex Green Woodcock (line 2484).
